member.name: T:BrowserApi.Css.Authoring.Selector
member.summary: Represents a CSS selector — the "which elements?" half of a CSS rule. Composes via C# operators that map to CSS combinators with carefully-chosen precedence.

remarks.para: is the universal currency for any rule's left-hand side: simple selectors (class, type, attribute), pseudo-classes (:hover, :focus), compound selectors (.card.active), complex selectors (.card > .title), and selector lists (.card, .panel). Every operator and fluent method returns a new so chains compose without intermediate types.

Operator precedence is chosen so that natural-looking expressions parse the way a CSS author expects. Compound (*) binds tightest — A * B > C means (A * B) > C, i.e. .a.b > .c. Selector list (|) binds loosest — A | B.Hover means A | (B.Hover), i.e. .a, .b:hover.

Pseudo-classes are exposed as instance properties (.Hover, .Focus, …) because in CSS they always attach to a selector, never stand alone. Pseudo-elements (.Before, .After) return a — a constrained type that disallows further pseudo-elements or descendants, since those would produce invalid CSS.
